result.question: I have to justify this quarter's maintenance budget for Transformer 1 at site MAIN. Give me an overall health index and condition category built from the latest dissolved gases plus the oil quality readings (dbds, interfacial_v, dielectric_rigidity, oxygen, nitrogen, co2). Then rank the transformer's known failure modes from most to least supported by the current evidence, with a short reason for each of the top three. Tell me how often we should resample the oil: monthly if the condition is poor or the top-ranked mode involves arcing, quarterly if it is fair, and annually if it is good. Check the work order history for any oil filtration or regeneration in the last year, and if there was one, say the gas-based ranking may be understated and recommend a re-baseline sample. If the health index can't be computed because an input is missing, don't guess. Base the ranking and interval on the DGA fault classification alone and say which input was missing.
result.answer:
Here's the budget justification package for **Transformer 1 (MAIN)**, based on the latest sample (2024-01-19):

## 1. Health Index

**Health Index: 72.4 / 100 — Condition: Good**

Built from all required inputs (DGA gases + oil quality): H2 2850, O2 5850, N2 27850, CH4 7400, CO 32, CO2 1340, C2H4 16650, C2H6 5470, C2H2 7 ppm; DBDS 19, power factor 1, interfacial tension 45 mN/m, dielectric rigidity 55 kV, water content 0. No inputs were missing.

*Note: the automated DGA interpretation service (IEC 60599 Rogers Ratio) was unavailable, so I computed the ratios directly: r1 = CH4/H2 = 2.60 (code 2), r2 = C2H2/C2H4 = 0.0004 (code 0), r3 = C2H4/C2H6 = 3.04 (code 3) → **thermal fault signature (T1–T2 range, ~150–700°C)**, no arcing. This is the standard deterministic calculation, not a guess.*

## 2. Failure Mode Ranking (most → least supported by current evidence)

| Rank | Failure Mode | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating** | Dominant heavy hydrocarbons (C2H4 16,650 ppm, CH4 7,400 ppm, C2H6 5,470 ppm) with negligible acetylene (7 ppm) — the classic oil-immersed thermal fault signature per the Rogers ratio result above. |
| **2** | **Thermal Fault — Core/Winding** | Same thermal gas profile could stem from a hot core or winding, but CO (32 ppm) and CO2 (1,340 ppm) are low, indicating cellulose is not involved — points to the oil rather than solid insulation as the hot zone. |
| **3** | **Tap Changer Mechanical Wear** | Corroborated by an open priority-1 PdM work order (WO 1000051) for OLTC inspection with suspected contact wear/coking — a known source of this exact thermal gas pattern. |
| 4 | Oil Dielectric Degradation | Dielectric rigidity (55 kV) and DBDS (19) are marginal; interfacial tension (45) acceptable — mildly supported. |
| 5 | Partial Discharge in Oil | H2 elevated, but the H2-to-hydrocarbon ratios favor thermal over PD. |
| 6 | Cellulose Insulation Ageing | CO/CO2 too low for cellulose degradation. |
| 7 | Low-Energy Arcing (Sparking) | C2H2 only 7 ppm — essentially absent. |
| 8 | High-Energy Arcing | No acetylene support whatsoever. |
| 9 | Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress | Water content measured at 0 — not supported. |

## 3. Resampling Interval

Condition is **Good** and the top-ranked mode is a thermal fault (not arcing) → **resample annually**, per your decision rule. (Caveat for the write-up: the elevated gas absolute levels mean trending the annual sample against these baselines is important — any uptick in C2H2 or H2 should trigger an immediate recheck.)

## 4. Work Order History Check (last 12 months)

Only one work order exists for this asset: **WO 1000051** (OLTC inspection, status WAPPR, PdM, priority 1). **No oil filtration or regeneration work order was found in the last year**, so no re-baseline sample is required and the gas-based ranking above is not understated by prior oil treatment.
